//: Every translation of the app's interface. Read by Scripts/build-catalog.py,
which writes the .xcstrings catalogues from it.
The translations live here rather than in the catalogues because that
generator rewrites those from scratch: anything not represented here would
be erased the next time somebody ran it, silently.
Terminology follows HoursCore/Export/ExportLanguage.swift wherever the two
overlap — the app and the timesheet it produces should not use two different
words for the same thing. Balance is Saldo (Solde in French), Expected is
Soll in German, Break is Pause.
Register is impersonal or imperative wherever that reads naturally, which
avoids choosing between du/Sie, tu/vous and ty/pan in nine languages at once.
Where a pronoun is unavoidable it is the informal one, except in French.
These are careful translations, not reviewed ones. A native speaker should
read at least German and Croatian before the app ships in them: the long
lines in Settings have a voice, and a voice is the first thing translation
loses.
widgetInterface names the subset the widget extension uses. The widget
ships its own catalogue, and giving it every app string would bloat an
extension that needs a few dozen.
watchInterface does the same for the Apple Watch app and its complications,
which share one catalogue in HoursWatchShared.
